A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMPO research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions to the experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original EMPO experiments on mathematical reasoning, TruthfulQA, and TriviaQA, together with training dynamics and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V3 reports original EMPO experiments, including natural-reasoning and Llama results, pass@k analyses, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The semantic-cluster rewards, advantage normalization, and entropy thresholds remain. V3 replaces DeBERTa-v3-large with the 1.5B General-Verifier for free-form clustering and removes KL regularization from Equation 7; v1 used a KL coefficient of 0.02 for free-form QA. These are localized component and loss changes within the existing EMPO procedure.

E1.justification: V1 trains and evaluates its non-mathematical models on TriviaQA and TruthfulQA. V3 removes those experiments, trains on Natural Reasoning across multiple subject domains, and evaluates on MMLU-Pro and GPQA. This substantially replaces the represented questions and task requirements, while retaining NuminaMath training and the main mathematical benchmark suite.

E2.justification: The non-mathematical comparison changes from Instruct models with and without zero-shot CoT to Base, five-shot Base, Instruct, SFT, and GRPO baselines in Table 2. The main mathematical comparator membership remains, but the reported GRPO reward now penalizes unextractable answers with -0.5 instead of 0.

E3.justification: Reported RL training changes from two to three epochs and from a learning rate of 3e-6 to 3e-7. Natural-reasoning experiments introduce Base initialization, a 14B configuration, filtered training data, 12 responses per prompt, shorter completion limits, and multiple-choice evaluation. Llama configurations, pass@k testing through k=256, and computational-cost protocols are added. These reported setting changes do not establish that the unchanged mathematical results were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds pass@k analyses examining whether RL improves sampling efficiency or reasoning coverage, runtime and memory comparisons, and a base-model reasoning case. It also reports Llama Base training failures and clustering-quality problems. V1's specific no-KL reward-hacking example and before/after UFO-answer case are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark results. Both already show shaded training-dynamics curves without specifying their statistical interpretation; v3's additional results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: TruthfulQA and TriviaQA result entries are removed and replaced by MMLU-Pro and GPQA results, including 50.1% and 28.8% for 7B EMPO. Llama accuracies, pass@k curves, and computational-cost measurements are new. These are results under different conditions, not direct improvements over v1's QA scores. Table 1's mathematical values remain unchanged; its accompanying prose corrects the 7B Instruct average from 48.1% to 49.4%.

T1.justification: Appendix F newly states an O(G^2 N) computational-complexity bound for semantic clustering. The semantic-entropy definitions remain, and no theorem or proof is added. Appendix I's discussion of non-identifiability is qualitative.

C1.justification: The central unsupervised reasoning claim remains, but v3 makes efficient selection of pre-existing reasoning pathways an explicit contribution and conclusion. V1 presented reliance on pretraining mainly as a conjecture. The headline non-mathematical claim also shifts from improving Instruct-model truthfulness to improving Base-model natural reasoning.

C2.justification: V3 develops a sampling-efficiency interpretation using pass@k and adds specific applicability limits involving Llama Base training and semantic-clustering quality. It explicitly explains the supervised auxiliary verifier's role within its claimed unsupervised framework and hypothesizes noisy references as a cause of SFT weakness. V1's separate KL-necessity discussion and code-generation limitation are removed.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and E-G add separate evaluation templates, clustering and verifier pseudocode, data-filtering code, per-model training recipes, hardware information, and resource measurements. V3 also supplies a project-code link and states that training configurations are released. These substantially expand documentation, although the PDFs alone cannot verify the external resources.

R1.justification: The existing three-part related-work discussion is largely retained. V3 adds a focused comparison with TTRL, distinguishing training/test separation and task scope, and cites recent work on RL's relationship to pretrained reasoning capabilities. Dataset and supporting-method references are updated, including removing the TruthfulQA and TriviaQA references.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements are rewritten, the discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten and combined, and reward-hacking discussion moves into the method section. The experimental narrative is revised, and the appendices are reorganized into a contents-listed set of topical sections. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 adds an introductory performance chart, redraws the method overview, reformats the training-dynamics plots, and adds pass@k figures. Table 2 is substantially redesigned, and new Llama, training-recipe, and resource tables appear. Prompt boxes are restyled and expanded, with new algorithm and code displays throughout the appendices.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's limited non-mathematical comparisons with supervised and few-shot baselines and empirically examines its pretraining hypothesis through pass@k. Llama failures and clustering limitations clarify applicability, while implementation and computational-cost disclosures substantially improve transparency. These gains outweigh the loss of TruthfulQA/TriviaQA coverage. Some reporting problems remain: Figure 4's caption names OMNI where the panel says AMC23, and Appendix F's batch-size description conflicts with Table 4.
